```{r, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

#read in data, should not show up on dashboard

library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

#data.fivethirtyeight.com / silver bulletin
#for prediction using data

# install.packages("fivethirtyeight")
library(fivethirtyeight)

candy <- fivethirtyeight::candy_rankings
# candy
candy <- candy |>
  mutate(type =
                case_when(
                          chocolate & fruity ~ "both", # ORDER MATTERS
                          chocolate ~ "chocolate",
                          fruity ~ "fruity",
                          .default = "other"
                          )
         )

# count(candy, type)
```

## Row 1

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Total Candies"

list(
  icon = "basket",
  color = "warning",
  value = nrow(candy) # number of rows in candy dataset (85)
)
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Number of Fruity Candies"

list(
  icon = "basket",
  color = "warning",
  ###number of rows in candy dataset (85)
  # value = count(candy, fruity == "TRUE") # 38; DOESN'T WORK SINCE IT OUTPUTS A TABLE, NOT A VALUE
  
  # value = nrow(candy[candy$fruity == "TRUE", ]) # 38; slow due to duplicating dataframe, AND if NA values exist, will be added to count
  
  value = sum(candy$type == "fruity") # 37 (Amber's solution); works because type is our newly made column that filters for 1) fruity + chocolate, 2) exclusively fruity, and 3) exclusively chocolate
  
  # value = sum(candy$fruity == "TRUE" & candy$chocolate == "FALSE", na.rm = TRUE) # 38 without the candy$chocolate condition, 37 with it
  
  
  
  # value = candy |>              # ALSO WORKS, ASK NIKKOS
  #   filter(type == "fruity") |>
  #   nrow()
)
```
